articles.title: Norris arrasa, Mercedes reina y Alonso no tiene premio en una carrera inolvidable
articles.standfirst: George Russell (4º) y Kimi Antonelli (5º) no suben al podio, pero sí certifican el título de constructores
articles.summary: George Russell (4º) y Kimi Antonelli (5º) no suben al podio, pero sí certifican el título de constructores
articles.body: La mejor carrera de la temporada 2026 de la Fórmula 1 llegó al 20º intento. El Gran Premio de Brasil resultó inolvidable, con condiciones climáticas locas, opciones de todo tipo y un guion imprevisible de inicio a fin. En la clase reina ya hay campeón y no queda título en juego tras la corona de Mercedes, pero la emoción no es discutible. Siempre existe. De Interlagos salió ganador un enorme Lando Norris tras ir de menos a más, con un recital de Max Verstappen a su lado (del 19º al 2º) y ningún premio para un Fernando Alonso valiente y mágico (12º). Porque en el maravilloso Interlagos siempre hay lugar a la magia. Que no llegó con un cielo cayéndose encima de los pilotos como en la clasificación, pero sí con un guion único en las condiciones mixtas y los giros en la historia cuando la pista paulista cambiaba. La traca final la puso un último chaparrón que Norris gestionó como nadie. También certifica el Mundial de Mercedes sin subir a un podio que ocuparon Verstappen y Hadjar. Cuando se consulte al ganador del 2026 en Brasil, muchos no recordarán que parecía la enésima fiesta del campeón Antonelli. Clavó la salida, lanzó su ataque ante Norris e hizo 20 vueltas perfectas. Pero cuando el asfalto se secó, el Mercedes se vino abajo. El italiano sufrió problemas de grip y un trompo en la curva 1 quitó toda su confianza de golpe. "El coche se va a un lado cuando acelero", reportaba. Perdió las posiciones de podio, y en el equipo dominador del año todo se torció en un abrir y cerrar de ojos. Porque no sólo sufrió Kimi ya que Russell se salió... en el pit lane. Rescataron un 4º del británico al acertar con el último intermedio y un 5º del campeón en serias dificultades. Así es la F1 cuando llueve. Su novena corona llegó de forma agria. No era lo que esperaban, desde luego. Y los focos de Sao Paulo van a Norris. El campeón saliente fue a más. No empezó bien, regaló posiciones y se rehizo con los secos. Nadie le igualaba, ni un Max Verstappen que firmó otro recital para el recuerdo en una de sus pistas favoritas. En la Fórmula 1 no siempre gana el mejor, aunque Lando sí que destacó en Brasil. El otro nombre destacado es el de Max. Salía al fondo de la parrilla y tras cinco giros ya había adelantado 15 posiciones. Tenía velocidad, medía riesgos y se disparó a puestos de podio con el caos de Antonelli. También en su equipo no dudaron, y permitieron que Hadjar le abriese la puerta para garantizar que los dos acompañaban en el cajón a Norris. No tuvo otro cambio de ritmo bajo el último diluvio, pero en Red Bull siguen sumando. Dos podios. Sin poder con el mejor Norris. Que honró el número 1 a lo grande, voló en cualquier condición y demuestra que es un dignísimo campeón de la Fórmula 1. También se engancha a la pelea del subcampeonato, aunque Verstappen está disparado ante el caos de unos Ferrari que no pasaron de un 7º (Leclerc) y 9º (Hamilton) entre trompos, falta de ritmo y las sanciones. En clave española, Brasil devolvió parte de la emoción que parecía robada. La puso Alonso, lanzado por unas condiciones en las que el AMR26 no es un coche tan problemático. No salió bien al encontrarse con el trallazo de Bearman, pero cuando los intermedios se hicieron añicos, voló. Cazó a los Ferrari sin ningún grip y firmó la pasada del día al dejar atrás a Lewis Hamilton. Fue un exterior, un adelantamiento puro que recuerda todo lo que vale el ovetense. Con un coche competente... Ese subidón en pista y una velocidad importante le devolvió a la batalla de los puntos, aunque la trazada se secaba y también recordó lo anticompetitivo del motor Honda. Cosa que Alonso quiso compensar con otro movimiento de puro piloto en un interior a Albon en la 7. Pero sin locura climática, el déficit de rendimiento es excesivo. Permitió incomodar a Lindblad o a los Alpine, pero el premio fue nulo pese al último chaparrón. Sí tenía velocidad y ritmo, pero faltó un golpe más de una fortuna que se escapó. Una verdadera lástima. Más gris resultó la carrera de Carlos Sainz. No pasó del 19º, sólo por delante de Cámara entre los que vieron meta. Pero sí que trató de luchar, especialmente en un inicio de carrera que le pegó a los puntos. Se colocó mejor que coches más rápidos, llegó a tener una breve batalla con Alonso y su carrera se complicó cuando los ritmos se estabilizaron. El madrileño buscó cambiar la dinámica con anticipación de su parada para los secos, pero el Williams encontró otro defecto en una falta de potencia alarmante. Se sabía que montaba una unidad bastante castigada y eso le dejó sin más batalla que ante los Haas y Pérez por no cerrar el paquete en carrera. Con el ritmo de carrera más lento tampoco existió anticipación a la lluvia final. No había ritmo ni ejecución, es la peor cara de una carrera preciosa.

articles.title: Sao Paulo Grand Prix result: Lando Norris wins as Mercedes secure constructors' championship
articles.summary: McLaren's Lando Norris wins a gripping Sao Paulo Grand Prix in difficult conditions, as Mercedes secure the 2026 constructors' championship.
articles.body:
McLaren's Lando Norris beat Max Verstappen to win a gripping Sao Paulo Grand Prix in which new world champion Kimi Antonelli and Mercedes team-mate George Russell both made critical mistakes in difficult conditions.

Norris, who started from pole, lost the lead to Antonelli at the start and dropped back when the track was wet.

But an earlier pit stop for dry-weather tyres put Norris on Antonelli's tail and the Italian spun away the lead at the first corner.

After reclaiming first place, Norris dominated through a late shower of rain which required a switch back to wet-weather tyres to take his first win since the Dutch Grand Prix at the end of August.

A few laps before Antonelli lost the lead, Russell, who started seventh, spun exiting the pits and lost 15 to 20 seconds after working his way back into podium contention.

Despite their travails, Russell and Antonelli finished fourth and fifth to clinch the constructors' championship for Mercedes a week after the Italian had tied up the drivers' title.

Norris had too much pace for Verstappen whether the track was dry or wet and stamped his authority on the race.

But the Dutchman put in another supreme drive in changeable conditions in Interlagos to take second after starting in 21st place.

An accomplished performance from Norris in a revived McLaren to take his first win for more than two months

A superb comeback from Verstappen from an engine penalty

A difficult day for both Mercedes, notwithstanding the greater glory of the constructors' win, and Ferrari in the tricky conditions

Norris brilliant in wet & Verstappen recovery extraordinary - driver ratings

Norris had started from his first pole position since the Spanish Grand Prix in September, but lost first place immediately after Antonelli, alongside him on the front row, leaped into the lead.

The new world champion pulled away to build a five-second advantage in 10 laps as he began to look as if he might crown his achievement with a win at the first attempt.

Antonelli's lead was more than eight seconds by lap 13 but the track was drying and three laps later Norris came in for dry-weather slick tyres.

The Italian followed him in a lap later, but Norris had gained so much time with his earlier stop that he was on the Mercedes' gearbox when it rejoined.

Antonelli defended for a couple of laps but he was complaining over the radio that the car felt strange under acceleration, and on lap 20 he lost control on the entry to Turn One, spinning and handing the lead to Norris.

That left Norris three seconds ahead of Hadjar with Verstappen now close behind Antonelli, who ran wide again at Turn One four laps later and handed third place to the Dutchman.

Hadjar had every bit as much pace as Verstappen, but was not as consistent and made too many mistakes, and within 10 laps the team leader was on the Frenchman's tail.

Red Bull ordered Hadjar to let Verstappen by on lap 39 in the hope the four-time champion could close on Norris.

But the Briton had too much pace and held off Verstappen, switching to another set of soft tyres before needing intermediates when the rain came down increasingly heavily in the final 10 laps.

Norris said: "It was a very tough race - very, very tough. Not the best of launches off the line, but a lot of challenges today with the conditions and going on slicks in the wet is always tough.

"The main thing today was that I just kept it cool and I did not make any mistakes. I had the pace when I needed to so it was good. Nice to be back on the top step and what a place to do it as well."

Verstappen had made speedy progress up from his position at the back.

Initially, Lewis Hamilton, who had started alongside the Red Bull, progressed faster, and was ninth by lap two, but Verstappen soon got into his stride and passed the Ferrari within a further two laps and continued his forward progress.

By lap 10, Verstappen was up to a remarkable sixth place and right behind the Racing Bulls of Liam Lawson, with Hadjar ahead chasing Russell, who by then was up to third after starting seventh.

But Russell dashed his own hopes when he stopped on lap 16, at the same time as Norris, and spun in the pit lane exit which mirrors on the inside of the track the run through the Senna S first two corners.

Russell was broadside in the pit lane as rivals squeezed past him left and right as he manoeuvred his way straight again and rejoined the race, now down in 10th.

After that, he drove well with strong pace to put himself back in contention and a fourth-place finish was a strong result in the circumstances.

He had more pace than Antonelli in the closing laps and the team ordered them to swap positions as they sealed their ninth constructors' title, and first since 2021.

Both Antonelli and and Charles Leclerc were handed five-second time penalties by the stewards for separate incidents after the race.

The penalty for an unsafe release does not affect Antonelli's fifth-place finish, but Ferrari's Leclerc drops to eighth for causing a collision late on with Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson, who is promoted to seventh.

McLaren's Oscar Piastri was sixth, nowhere near Norris' pace, while Hamilton took ninth.

After his initial burst up the field, the seven-time champion lacked pace, despite pushing correctly for an early stop for slicks, and could make no more ground.

Although leading Leclerc for much of the race, Hamilton fell behind him with his second stop for slicks, while Leclerc hung on for the change to intermediates to consolidate his position.

Audi's Nico Hulkenberg took the final point for 10th place.

The season is due to end with a final triple header, starting with the Las Vegas Grand Prix. The night race is due to start at 04:00 GMT on Sunday, 22 November.

articles.title: Alonso: "Con lluvia peleamos con Ferrari y Mercedes, gran sensación"
articles.standfirst: Con intermedios fue remontando en el inicio y pasó a Hamilton, luego con las gomas de seco, sus opciones se acabaron
articles.summary: Con intermedios fue remontando en el inicio y pasó a Hamilton, luego con las gomas de seco, sus opciones se acabaron
articles.body: El 12º final de Alonso en el Gran Premio de Brasil le supo a poco, sobre todos porque cuando la pista estuvo mojada, al principio y al final, su ritmo estaba como para luchar por llegar a los puntos. Su adelantamiento a Hamilton en el inicio de la prueba, como ya sucedió en Sepang, muestra lo que necesita Fernando para estar con los mejores, que es más potencia en el coche. Cuando todo se iguala en ese sentido, emerge como siempre. "Sin duda, fue mejor bajo la lluvia que en seco, Creo que el ritmo fue bastante bueno, lo cual fue una grata sorpresa. El coche funcionó bien durante toda la carrera. Es evidente que todavía nos falta mucha velocidad punta en las rectas, algo difícil de compensar; sin embargo, en ciertos momentos, al principio, en nuestra lucha con los Ferrari, e incluso al final frente a los Mercedes fuimos competitivos", resumía Fernando "Teniendo en cuenta lo mucho que perdemos en las rectas, esto significa que el coche se comportó de forma fenomenal en las curvas; fue una sensación muy positiva", añadía alabando las condiciones de un chasis que con un buen motor puede dar mucho de sí en 2027. "En general, la carrera fue mejor que el resto del fin de semana. En los entrenamientos libres no estábamos del todo satisfechos con el coche, pero en la carrera logramos encontrar un mejor punto de equilibrio. Veremos qué podemos hacer en la próxima cita", decía ya sobre Las Vegas, que es el peor que les queda por las largas rectas. "No hay nada nuevo que aprender sobre el coche a estas alturas; ya estamos en la vigésima primera carrera, así que sabemos exactamente qué aspectos debemos mejorar", cerraba el '14' sobre este final de temporada.

articles.title: Ni la lluvia da opciones a Sainz: "Estamos corriendo en una situación muy complicada"
articles.standfirst: El español finalizó 19º, su peor resultado en una carrera en la que vio la meta
articles.summary: El español finalizó 19º, su peor resultado en una carrera en la que vio la meta
articles.body: Carlos Sainz no pudo aprovechar un loco Gran Premio de Brasil. Ni en la clasificación, perjudicada por la bandera roja que causó Rafael Cámara. Ni en carrera, sin capacidad de poder cambiar el paso al llegar tarde al último cambio a intermedios pese a anticipar en la monta de secos. Para más inri, tampoco había potencia en su motor. Cruzó la meta 19º, lejos de cualquier opción. Su peor resultado en la F1 en cualquier carrera en la que ha terminado, un resumen de un año para olvidar y pensar en la reacción de su equipo en 2027. "Fue una carrera rara, complicada... pero rara a nivel personal. Degradé mucho el neumático delantero en el primer stint y es algo que tenemos que entender. En el último stint fue al revés y fui mucho más rápido. Pero salió una carrera con tráfico, banderas azules... y es difícil porque vamos lentos, nos doblan, se enfría el neumático y lo calientas pero te vuelven a doblar", valoró el español en DAZN. La tónica de un curso en el que el rendimiento en Williams no está. Cosa que Sainz sabe y no le hace ninguna gracia, lógicamente. "La situación en la que estamos corriendo es muy complicada", lanzó. Poco consuelo quedará en Las Vegas, Qatar y Abu Dhabi, las tres paradas que quedan para el final del curso 2026. "Tenemos que seguir aprendiendo y en carrera aprendí. El primer stint fue tan difícil que casi que aprendí porque probé cosas al final de carrera que sí que me funcionaron", señaló. Pero es poco consuelo, lógico. Sí intentó luchar y en carrera volvió a repetir una buena arrancada. Se lanzó ante Piastri, llegó a la altura de Albon y aprovechó el toque entre Bearman y Alonso para ganar la posición en la primera recta. Pero su ritmo decayó sumando unos problemas de potencia que llevan permaneciendo durante todo el fin de semana. Más allá de ese inicio, Sainz pudo adelantar a Stroll y no encontró una gran respuesta en el paso por boxes. Irá a Las Vegas, una carrera en la que brilló en 2025 con una gran clasificación, con el objetivo de recuperar buenas sensaciones. No han aparecido demasiado esta temporada y desde Bakú regresan los problemas a un equipo Williams que piensa en 2027 desde hace muchos meses.

articles.title: Sao Paulo Grand Prix: Harry Benjamin's driver ratings as Lando Norris wins at Interlagos
articles.summary: BBC Radio 5 Live F1 commentator Harry Benjamin rates how the drivers performed during the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.
articles.body:
McLaren's Lando Norris secured his third win of the season on Sunday by beating Max Verstappen to victory at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.

Norris started on pole position but lost the lead of the wet-dry-wet race to new world champion Kimi Antonelli on the opening lap. But after an early pit stop for dry tyres, he regained control when Mercedes' Antonelli spun at the first corner.

Verstappen, meanwhile, claimed his eighth consecutive podium with another eye-catching drive in tricky conditions at Interlagos, while his Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar finished third.

Here are my ratings for how the drivers performed across the whole weekend in Brazil.

Pretty difficult to ask for much more for the McLaren driver. Fastest in first practice on Friday, brilliant in the wet to take pole and then kept his head through constantly changing conditions to win comfortably. Losing the lead at the start was only a minor blemish.

Another extraordinary recovery drive in the Red Bull. Fastest in final practice and then charged from 21st to second, making up 10 places almost immediately, and once again looking completely at home in difficult conditions.

One of his strongest weekends all season. Qualified well, ran with team-mate Verstappen for much of the race and delivered another podium despite a few mistakes along the way. Had the pace to make Red Bull think before eventually letting Verstappen through.

The pace was excellent all weekend and second in qualifying showed what was possible, even if his engine penalty dropped him to seventh. Spinning his Mercedes on the pit exit was a huge error and probably cost him a podium, but recovering to fourth was a very strong response.

For the opening stint this looked like the perfect first race as world champion. A brilliant start and built a healthy lead, but spinning it away after switching to the slick tyres unlocked a messy afternoon.

Another weekend where things never really clicked. His qualifying result was compromised by the timing of the red flag, but he was a long way from Norris' pace in the race and finished almost a minute behind his McLaren team-mate.

An excellent weekend in the Racing Bulls. Qualified fifth, started third and even ran second during the opening stages before eventually slipping backwards as the race developed.

A very good recovery from 14th on the grid after his power-unit penalty. Qualified fourth on pure pace and worked his way through to eighth. He passed Lawson towards the end but was given a five-second penalty for hitting the New Zealander, which means he finishes behind him.

The opening few laps were vintage Hamilton as he charged from 20th to ninth, but the progress then stalled. He struggled for pace in the Ferrari on the intermediate tyres, and a late spin capped a race where more looked possible after such a promising start.

Outstanding in the wet qualifying session to put Audi sixth before penalties promoted him to fourth. A 10-second time penalty for going off track in his battle with Franco Colapinto hurt his Sunday, but he still came away with the final point.

Norris wins gripping race after Antonelli and Russell errors

Norris sparkles in Sao Paulo despite firework mishap

His qualifying was cut short by a mechanical problem in his Racing Bulls and further power-unit changes left him starting well down the order. Recovered well to 11th and came extremely close to points.

Reaching Q3 for the first time this season was a big positive and he raced well enough to even get ahead of Hamilton with a spectacular move in the Aston Martin. P12 doesn't look spectacular, but there was plenty to like about the weekend.

Alpine struggled badly in the wet qualifying session but Colapinto made a reasonable recovery. Finished ahead of team-mate Pierre Gasly and was involved in the battle with Hulkenberg that eventually earned the Audi driver a penalty.

A disappointing weekend after both Alpines went out in Q1. Made a little progress from 16th on the grid but finished behind Colapinto and never really threatened the points.

Saturday was the highlight after reaching Q3 for the first time this season and earning ninth on the grid. Unfortunately the race went the opposite way and he fell back to 15th in the Williams.

Showed good speed before qualifying but his crash in the Audi in Q1 put him on the back foot for his home race.

A really strong Saturday to put the Haas eighth in qualifying and sixth on the grid. The race was a completely different story, though, as he tumbled out of contention and eventually finished 17th.

Starting last because of his engine penalty made it difficult from the outset. Kept his nose clean, picked up several positions in his Cadillac and reached the finish ahead of a Williams and a Haas.

Unlucky to have his Q2 attempt interrupted by the red flag just as he switched to the intermediates, but Sunday offered little recovery.

Plenty of raw speed on his F1 debut in the Haas but plenty of learning too. Reaching Q2 in those conditions was impressive, although two qualifying incidents and a difficult race ultimately left him 20th.

Out in Q1 and never looked capable of matching Aston Martin team-mate Alonso across the weekend.

Only 20th in qualifying before being promoted a couple of places on the grid. His race was over before it had even begun, with Cadillac retiring his car with a technical problem, so Sunday itself is impossible to judge.

articles.title: Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari driver says he overrode team's pit call due to 'lack of information' provided as rain fell during Sao Paulo GP
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton finished ninth in the Sao Paulo Grand Prix as Ferrari endured a disappointing weekend in Brazil; Hamilton lost out late in the race after ignoring a call to come into the pits to switch from slick to intermediate tyres as rain intensified
articles.body:
Hamilton was running in eighth at Interlagos when heavy rain began to fall with 10 laps to go. While the leaders had already passed the pit entry by the time the rain intensified, Mercedes brought in George Russell from fifth.

Ferrari instructed Hamilton to come in, but he decided to do the opposite to the car just in front of him at the time, Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson. Hamilton's team-mate Charles Leclerc, running just behind him, came into the pits.

The seven-time world champion spun on the next lap in the treacherous conditions, before pitting at the end of it to follow his rivals onto intermediates.

While there was little at stake, as Hamilton ultimately finished ninth rather than claiming what could have been seventh if he had got past Lawson, it was the latest example of imperfect execution from the British driver and his Italia team.

Speaking to Sky Italy after the race, Hamilton said: "The last bit of information I got was that the rain was going to stay the same, and in those conditions my grip was feeling pretty good.

"And I was like, 'ah, I'm catching.' And I was coming out the last corner, just before the pit lane they asked me to box, and I was right behind Lawson.

"He went in, and I ended up staying (out). They didn't say it's raining more in the first half of the lap. If I'd have known that I would have come in.

"As soon as I got to Turn 1, I realised it was wet. So, it just lacked a little bit of information there.

"And ultimately, that's on me. Sorry for the team, for that. I gave it everything. We just didn't have the pace today unfortunately."

Hamilton had come into the weekend off the back of a major controversy with his team-mate in Mexico last weekend, as he was angered by a first-lap clash between the pair that he felt cost him victory and the team a one-two.

While Hamilton revealed on Saturday that the pair had "squashed" their issues, the precious nature of their winning opportunity in Mexico City was highlighted by their struggles in Brazil.

Both Hamilton and Leclerc were compromised by grid penalties that saw them start from 20th and 14th, respectively, but neither appeared to have the pace to match McLaren's race winner Lando Norris or Red Bull's Max Verstappen in second.

Hamilton told Sky Sports F1 : "Really tough day and weekend for the whole team. They have done a really great job.

"All the mechanics did such a great job switching out the engine and making sure the car was as good as it could be."

Hamilton had a great start as he climbed to ninth on the first lap, and successfully pulled off being the first driver to switch from intermediates to slicks as the track dried early in the race, but didn't have the pace to take advantage of either moment.

He added: "We struggled in the dry but I had a great start. Unfortunately, the rear tyres just ballooned and overheated and I struggled.

"After that, I was pushing to go onto the slicks, which I eventually got on, I think I was one of the earlier ones [to switch to that tyre].

"I was feeling pretty good. It was very tricky in those conditions. We ended up having an extra stop, which ultimately, I had a lot of ground to cover there."

articles.title: Toto Wolff 'proud' of Mercedes turnaround after winning F1 2026 Constructors' Championship at Sao Paulo Grand Prix
articles.summary: Mercedes won their ninth F1 Constructors' Championship with three races to spare of the 2026 season; Mercedes won eight in a row between 2014 and 2021 before a fallow period and Toto Wolff is particularly proud of how the Silver Arrows bounced back
articles.body:
Mercedes won their ninth constructors' title on Sunday at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, five years after their last championship, which was their eighth in a row at the time.

Regulation changes in 2022 ended Mercedes' dominance as they struggled to get on top of the so-called ground effect cars, but they have won the first season of the new 2026 cars, and also wrapped up the Drivers' Championship earlier this month with Kimi Antonelli.

"The thing is when you are in these difficult moments, like we all are sometimes in our lives, it's not that easy to keep going," said Wolff.

"Looking back in retrospect, you're saying, 'we needed these tough moments in order to grow as people or to grow as an organisation'. But when you're down, that is quite difficult to feel.

"I think those last four years were very difficult between getting it wrong, then kind of understanding why it was wrong and then realising no we didn't understand. That was a bit back and forth.

"But we will be looking back in 10 or 20 years. When you look at the statistics, it wasn't that we were complete losers over those four years, because we finished second, (second), third, fourth [in the championship], we won races, won many races. So it wasn't that bad at all when you look at the sheer numbers, but it felt not good."

As Wolff points out, Mercedes still won races between 2022 and 2025, with George Russell and Lewis Hamilton winning seven Grands Prix between them.

"The resilience of the team, the people that held together in those tough times, is a factor, I think," continued Wolff.

"It feels really good sealing those two titles. Not many sports teams have done that after consecutive run of championships, then a difficult spell and then coming back, so I'm really proud that we are part of this very small group of teams that have done that in all sports."

Mercedes move level with Williams on nine constructors' titles - only McLaren (10) and Ferrari (16) have more in Formula 1 history.

Wolff says his pride comes from the hard work in Mercedes' UK factories in Brackley and Brixworth to produce the best car, on average, this season.

"Sometimes the drivers, or myself, we are so visible because we are in in front of the TV cameras, but there's so many people that are part of this," he told Sky Sports F1 .

"I always say there are not two superstars, the drivers, but there are 2,500 superstars, all of them delivering a great job, being all of us contributing to such a championship."

Mercedes were unable to finish with either of their drivers on the podium in Brazil as Lando Norris dominated in mixed conditions, while Antonelli and Russell both spun.

Russell finished in fourth, just ahead of Antonelli who says everyone at Mercedes "deserves" this year's success.

"They have done an incredible year and it's an amazing group of people, who push every day to do their best and give us the best opportunity to fight for wins and championships," the Italian told Sky Sports F1 .

"This year they have done an incredible job and that's why they deserve this championship and we will enjoy it together."

Russell added: "We achieved what we came here to do and won the Constructors' Championship. We would have liked to have done it in a bit more style, but it's an incredible achievement for everyone in the team.

"We've had four difficult years and the whole organisation put so much work into getting us back into this position. When I joined Mercedes in 2022, we hoped we'd be fighting for championships regularly, so to have gone through that journey and now get back to the top is something we should all be incredibly proud of."

articles.title: Sao Paulo Grand Prix: Lando Norris sparkles in race that challenged drivers to their very limits
articles.summary: Apart from getting too close to a firework, Lando Norris was virtually impeccable during a Sao Paulo Grand Prix that challenged the drivers to their very limits.
articles.body:
Showing off on the podium after winning the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, Lando Norris made his first misstep of an afternoon that had challenged the Formula 1 drivers to their very limits.

Norris jumped off the top step, and tried to do his signature move, where he uncorks the champagne bottle by bashing it into the ground.

Except that, not for the first time, the force of his jump pushed things too far, and he smashed the bottle.

Then, holding up the shattered top to the crowd below, he stepped backwards and inadvertently put the side of his head into the sparkles blowing up from the fireworks on the front of the platform.

Red Bull drivers Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar showed no pity, and proceeded to drench him with the contents of their bottles.

In any case, Norris was fine, McLaren team principal Andrea Stella confirmed shortly afterwards, and the Briton showed no ill effects in his post-race interviews.

It was, he said, "one of the hardest races of the year in terms of focus needed every lap and therefore one of the best".

Norris wins gripping race after Antonelli and Russell errors

Norris brilliant in wet & Verstappen recovery extraordinary - driver ratings

Interlagos did what it often can, and threw everything at the drivers. The race started on a wet track, which dried progressively. There was more rain at the end.

Through it all, Norris was virtually impeccable. He made new world champion Kimi Antonelli look fallible for pretty much the first time all year, and then fended off what at one point was threatening to be one of those days when Verstappen appears to have descended from the Gods.

It says a lot for Norris' performance that it overshadowed Verstappen's drive from 21st on the grid to finish second.

Actually, perhaps the race had also started with a small blemish from the man who has had to hand his title of world champion to Antonelli this year without ever really being able to defend it.

Starting from pole, Norris was relatively slow away, at least compared with the Italian, and Antonelli blasted into a lead that for a while looked as if he would not lose.

But after the Mercedes driver had built an eight-second advantage in the first 13 laps, Norris began to come back at him as the track dried.

Stopping for slick tyres a lap before Antonelli cut a seven-second deficit to nothing, and when three laps later the new champion spun at Turn One under pressure from the old, Norris was promoted into a lead that he never again looked like losing.

"A lot was thrown at everyone on a day like today, but it was probably one of our best races in terms of execution and pit stops, timing of things," Norris said.

"We boxed one lap early on to the slicks. I came out and was right behind him and forced him to push a little bit more, and obviously he went into a mistake and I could capitalise on it.

"So, in terms of always being there where we needed to be, being able to put people under pressure was a very good day for that.

"Also, from my side, just not making any mistakes, which is so easy to do on a day like today. So, great performance from the whole team. Certainly up there with one of the best I've ever had."

For both Norris and McLaren, it was a welcome return to form. They started the year slowly, having fallen behind in development on their 2026 car as they diverted resources to ensure they got their title double over the line last year.

By mid-summer, they had caught up, and Norris took two consecutive wins either side of the summer break, and was unlucky not to get another in Madrid in September.

But then other teams overtook them again and McLaren have toiled relatively in recent races, especially in qualifying.

But the combination in Sao Paulo of some new parts, the circuit characteristics suiting them, and Norris excelling in the wet in qualifying and race, put him back in the game.

In so doing, he provided a performance that served as a reminder that he has been one of the drivers of the year, even if his equipment has not always met his exalted standards.

Stella said: "When Lando operates at his best, he's definitely one of the best drivers on the grid.

"We have seen that in these conditions, like yesterday (in qualifying), it's not the first time that when you have mixed variable conditions, he kind of is one of the fastest in finding the limit.

"And you have seen this today as well, when the track was in the middle between dry and wet. It was when he was probably gaining most throughout the races on anybody else.

"He's very sensitive in understanding how much grip is available. And very, I would say, even complete as a driver, despite he's still many years ahead of him, from a technical point of view, in terms of understanding how to deploy his tools to use the grip that is available, or to adapt to the balance of the car, because you're never going to have a really perfect car.

"You're never going to have the perfect conditions. So adaptability is actually probably the most important feature that you may want to possess as a driver. When there's a need to understand what's best, how to operate, he's definitely a master."

Verstappen raced with a car 'not in good shape'

For a time, it looked as if Verstappen might be in the running for a win.

A penalty for using too many engines this year left the four-time champion four places lower than the position from which he had won in similar slippery conditions at Interlagos two years ago.

So when he was up to fifth, and less than 15 seconds behind leader Antonelli, by the time the pit stops for dry tyres were looming on lap 15, with 56 still to go and more rain predicted, it looked ominous.

But once on to the slicks, Verstappen was not a threat to Norris on pace, even when heavy rain returned in the closing laps.

"That first stint went really, really well," Verstappen said. "We got very quickly back into the top 10, and the pace wasn't bad.

"But as soon as I switched to the slicks, I had an extreme amount of oversteer in the car in the high-speed corners, which made it super difficult to drive.

"So, we need to understand if something broke on the car, some kind of aero loss or whatever, because this was not normal.

"I sit here, of course, very happy with second, but at the same time, I know there was more in it if the car had been in good shape.

"Unfortunately, that was not the case. I actually did most of the race with a car that was not in good shape, and to finish second, of course, is fantastic.

"Maybe next year I'd love to start a bit further up front instead of starting from the back or the pit lane."

Mercedes back on top - but Wolff not expecting era of dominance

For a time, Antonelli looked set to celebrate clinching the title and becoming F1's youngest ever champion a week before in Mexico with a win.

But his most uncharacteristic spin ended that hope, and took him out of contention.

"Very disappointing because we were on for the win up to that point," he said.

"Also in this slicks, once I was able to get some temperature, I was getting to the rhythm, but yeah, the spin came, which still is something I need to look at because I don't know why I lost the rear so quickly as well, like no warning, nothing."

It was another bad day for team-mate George Russell, too, who had done excellent work to move up to third place right behind Norris after starting seventh.

He looked the one driver able to threaten Norris for raw pace, but his afternoon unravelled even before Antonelli's, when he spun exiting the pits and turned a 1.2-second deficit to the McLaren into 20. That was it for his hopes of a win.

Still, a fourth and a fifth place for Russell and Antonelli at the end was more than enough for Mercedes to clinch the constructors' championship. It was the team's ninth - but their first since 2021, after a difficult time through the last rule set.

Antonelli said: "I'm going to put all this aside for now because the team, you know, take the title, we take the title for the team and they all deserve it.

"I'm very proud to be part of this group and this team who has done and still does so much for me and I'm very happy for them."

Like Antonelli, team boss Toto Wolff was as focused on the lessons of the day and year as he was on the success.

He reflected on the fact that while Mercedes had dominated the first half of the season, not only have they been caught in the second, but upgrades brought to the car a few races ago did not have the expected effect.

"Look at the last few races," Wolff said. "We haven't won.

"Then today at the beginning of the race, Kimi was just storming away. It looked like this could be ours. But the competition has been getting tougher between Ferrari, McLaren, Red Bull and ourselves.

"It's four teams that can win races and will be challenging for a world championship. And I have no doubt that this is going to be very difficult for us next year."

Wolff is pleased that Mercedes have found their way back to the front after struggling relatively through what was known as the ground-effect era.

But he says he does not expect this to be the start of another dominant era such as they enjoyed with Lewis Hamilton in the last decade.

"Looking back, those last four years were very difficult between getting it wrong and then kind of understanding why it was wrong and then realising, no, we didn't understand. And that was a bit back and forth," he said.

"It wasn't that bad at all when you look at the sheer numbers, but it felt not good. And the resilience of the team, the people that held together in those tough times is a factor.

"So it feels really good sealing those two titles. Not many sports teams have done that after consecutive run of championships, then a difficult spell and then coming back.

"It looks like the most maybe competitive era that is about to start, because the teams have become so professional in capability, in resource, that this kind of runaway seasons, I don't see them any more, whether it's four in a row or eight in a row. And that is a completely new challenge.

"You can see how quickly it goes from being dominant. And within a few races, you realise that your upgrade doesn't work and you fall back and you're just third on the road.

"It's great for the sport. I wished it was the era of Mercedes and me running away with another few championships. I don't think it's the reality."

articles.title: NASCAR phenom Kyle Larson wins 2nd consecutive Cup Series title
articles.summary: Kyle Larson is now a three-time NASCAR champion after becoming the first back-to-back winner since 2010.
articles.body: Kyle Larson is now a three-time NASCAR champion. Larson clinched his third Cup Series title in six years early in the 400-mile season finale at Homestead-Miami Speedway on Sunday. He became the first back-to-back champion since Jimmie Johnson in 2010; Johnson won five in a row beginning in 2006. The 34-year-old Larson also became the 11th driver in NASCAR history with three Cup titles, joining a list that includes seven-time champs Richard Petty, Dale Earnhardt and Johnson. Jeff Gordon has four. Lee Petty, David Pearson, Cale Yarborough. Darrell Waltrip, Tony Stewart and Joey Logano have three. Ryan Blaney won the race for Team Penske, passing Tyler Reddick of 23XI Racing with a little more than a lap to go and with NBA legend Michael Jordan watching from pit road. Reddick finished second, followed by William Byron, Christopher Bell, Bubba Wallace and Denny Hamlin. The real celebration awaited Larson, who finished 12th. He immediately stopped near the start-finish line for a smoky burnout and then exchanged high-fives and hugs with his team and his kids. He climbed atop his No. 5 Chevy with the championship flag and all three kids to celebrate. He was the overwhelming favorite to hoist the Bill France Cup in Homestead long before the green flag dropped. He entered the weekend with a 67-point lead over Bell and needed only nine points to wrap up the title. He got one point for starting the race and seven more by finishing fourth in the opening stage. But because Bell didn’t win the opening stage, he had no path to catch Larson the rest of the day. Larson responded to crew chief Cliff Daniels dropping the news over the radio by saying, “That was anticlimactic.” Hendrick Motorsports owner Rick Hendrick, who notched his 16th Cup title, radioed Larson to congratulate him during the caution following the stage. “Now you can go ride the wall,” Hendrick joked. Larson did and ended up cutting a right-rear tire and having to pit out of sequence. It cost him any chance he had of winning the race. “I got the word that we clinched it, and I started driving like an idiot,” Larson said. “I’m more mad at myself.” Regardless, Larson put himself in position for the title with a historic postseason, dubbed NASCAR’s Chase for the championship. He ended a 51-race winless skid by winning three of the previous nine playoff events and finished in the top 10 in eight of them. He enjoyed a similar finish while winning it all in 2021, his first season at Hendrick. He won four of the last five races — including the finale at Phoenix Raceway — while still dealing with questions about how his time ended at Chip Ganassi Racing. His second title came in stunning fashion last year at Phoenix. He took advantage of a late caution — his crew put on two new tires instead of four — and leaped sentimental favorite Denny Hamlin on pit road with two laps to go. Hamlin didn’t have enough time to catch Larson. Larson’s third title was far less shocking. Securing the title was so much of a slam dunk that Larson was the only Cup driver invited to NASCAR’s championship media day Thursday, leading to a parade event that Larson called awkward. The biggest question was how Larson and his No. 5 Hendrick Motorsports team would handle the pressure. Larson put that to rest during qualifying Saturday. “They were debating on if a hot dog is a sandwich and if cereal is a soup,” Larson said. “So I would say they were pretty relaxed. I was surprised by all that.” A better question: How does Larson compare to the best drivers in motorsports history? Parnelli Jones, Mario Andretti, A.J. Foyt and Tony Stewart are widely regarded as the best of the best, guys who proved their worth by winning across varying racing series. Jones won in sprint cars and stock cars around the same time he won the 1963 Indianapolis 500. Andretti won four IndyCar titles, the 1967 Daytona 500 and the 1969 Indianapolis 500. Foyt won four Indy 500s and the 1972 Daytona 500. Stewart won the 1997 IndyCar championship, three Cup Series titles and is currently racing dragsters at the top level, the NHRA. Larson raced twice at the Indy 500 and has won the Rolex 24 at Daytona, three Chili Bowls and four Knoxville Nationals. And now he’s in elite company with three Cup titles. “He wins in everything he does, and they’re all completely different cars and tracks,” retired driver and current NBC Sports race analyst Jeff Burton said. “And he’s racing against the best in every discipline.”
